title: to_shouty_snake_case is not idempotent: full uppercase mapping emits combining marks that are then treated as word boundaries
property: converting an already shouty-snake-case string again leaves it unchanged (f(f(x)) == f(x)); output contains only alphanumerics and '_'
input: "ΐ" (U+0390 GREEK SMALL LETTER IOTA WITH DIALYTIKA AND TONOS)
expected: Output is a stable SHOUTY_SNAKE_CASE string; converting it again returns the same string
actual: First call gives "Ι\u{308}\u{301}" (word containing combining marks, which are not alphanumeric); second call splits at the marks and returns "Ι"
evidence: lib.rs: 'Word boundaries are defined by non-alphanumeric characters' and the library is 'intended to be unicode aware, internally consistent'. The uppercase() helper uses char::to_uppercase (full mapping) per word, producing non-alphanumeric combining characters inside a word, so the output of the conversion is itself re-segmented differently. Shouty-snake output of already-shouty input is expected to be a fixed point (cf. test6 SHOUTY_SNAKE_CASE => SHOUTY_SNAKE_CASE).
